label: zendesk ticket
title: zendesk-{num}
prompt: Read this zendesk ticket ({url}), summarize it here and in a ZENDESK-{num}.md file. List any attachments on the ticket and tell me whether there are any, then ask me which to download. Then let's figure out how you and I can make a plan to answer the customer.
notes: Any <sub>.zendesk.com and any path in front of /tickets/<num>, as gwt takes them. The url names no repository, so a pasted ticket opens in a zendesk-{num} worktree of the default repo, openziti/ziti-tunnel-sdk-c, which is gwt's default: tickets are usually tunneler issues. Shift+Enter picks another repo, or none for a scratch folder. No fetch: the agent reads the ticket through the zendesk tools it already has, and atrium holds no zendesk credential.

label: discourse topic
title: discourse-{num}
prompt: Read this discourse topic ({url}), summarize the question and what has been tried so far. Then let's figure out how you and I can make a plan to answer it.
notes: /t/<slug>/<id>, /t/<id> and a trailing post number all resolve to the topic id. Any <forum>.discourse.group. It opens in the default repo, openziti/ziti, like gwt does. Shift+Enter picks another repo, or none. A link with no number is the next row's.

label: discourse topic, linked without its number
title: discourse-{num}
prompt: Read this discourse topic ({url}), summarize the question and what has been tried so far. Then let's figure out how you and I can make a plan to answer it.
notes: /t/<slug> alone. Discourse redirects it to /t/<slug>/<id>, so the redirect fetch follows the link, as gwt does, and reads the topic id off the address it lands on. When it cannot, the directory says {num} and the dialog says why.
